problem.statement: The cost of housing in London is too high for people on ordinary incomes.
problem.who_bears_it: Private renters in London on median or below-median household incomes.

observable_condition.statement: Median private rent in London takes about a third of median gross household income.
observable_condition.metric: Median monthly rent as a share of median gross monthly household income, London

outcome_sought.statement: Median private rent in London falls to no more than 30 per cent of median gross household income.
outcome_sought.metric: Median monthly rent as a share of median gross monthly household income, London

causal_chain.cause: New homes in London are completed more slowly than new households form.

Small sites (under 0.25 hectares) deliver fewer homes than their planned share because the fixed pre-construction cost of a scheme (planning, surveys, design, utilities) is high relative to a scheme of two to ten homes.
causal_chain.effect: Fewer homes are completed than the plan assumes.

causal_chain.cause: Each small-site scheme buys a bespoke pre-construction package because no standard, pre-accepted package exists for common site types.
causal_chain.effect: The fixed pre-construction cost per scheme stays high.

intervention_point.statement: Replace the bespoke pre-construction package with a standard package that a borough has accepted in advance for a defined site type.
intervention_point.why_here: L1 and L2 need policy or land-market change that a private venture cannot supply within the constraints. L3 is a cost structure a private venture can change on its own.

prime_commercial_opportunity.customer: Small builders and SME developers building schemes of two to ten homes on small sites in London.
prime_commercial_opportunity.customer_observable_condition: A small scheme spends 12 to 18 months and £60,000 to £90,000 on pre-construction work before any revenue, and may still be refused consent.
prime_commercial_opportunity.core_functionality: Takes a small site of a defined type to a buildable consent for a fixed price and a fixed time, using a standard package the borough has accepted in advance.

outcome_link.mechanism: Lower fixed cost per scheme makes more small sites viable, so more homes are completed, so rents rise more slowly than they otherwise would.
outcome_link.scale_assumption: 500 schemes a year at six homes each, 3,000 additional homes a year, sustained for ten years.
outcome_link.contribution_unit: ratio points off the rent-to-income ratio by 2035
outcome_link.arithmetic: 3,000 homes a year for ten years = 30,000 homes = 0.8 per cent of a London stock of about 3.7 million. With a rent response of about minus 1.5 per cent for each 1 per cent of extra stock, rents fall about 1.2 per cent. 0.35 x 0.012 = 0.004, rounded to 0.005. The gap to target is 0.05, so this venture alone closes about a tenth of it.

requirements.statement: Deliver a buildable consent for a small site at a cost per scheme well below the bespoke route.
requirements.bottleneck: Every scheme pays for its own architect, planner and surveys, so professional hours per scheme do not fall with volume.
requirements.intervention: Sort small sites into a small number of site types and reuse one standard package per type, so most professional hours are spent once per type rather than once per scheme.
requirements.verification: Cost 20 synthetic schemes through the standard route and the bespoke route and confirm the standard route costs at least 40 per cent less per scheme.

requirements.statement: Remove the developer's doubt that a small scheme will get consent.
requirements.bottleneck: Consent risk sits with each scheme, so the developer discounts the value of any pre-construction package.
requirements.intervention: Agree the standard package with the borough in advance for each site type, so consent risk sits with the standard and not the site.
requirements.verification: Ten developer interviews in which the developer states a price for the package with and without borough pre-acceptance; the difference is the value of R2.

components.name: Site-type library
components.purpose: Classifies a small site into one of a fixed set of types with known constraints.

components.name: Standard pre-construction package
components.purpose: The design, planning and survey package reused for every site of a type.

components.name: Borough pre-acceptance agreement
components.purpose: The borough's advance acceptance of the standard package for a site type, so a conforming scheme gets consent on a fixed timetable.

evidence.claim: Median private rent in London is about 35 per cent of median gross household income.
evidence.source_or_test: Check against the ONS private rental affordability release for England, London row, latest year.
evidence.falsification_test: The ONS figure for London differs from 0.35 by more than 0.03.

evidence.claim: London completes fewer homes a year than its plan target.
evidence.source_or_test: Check GLA housing completions against the London Plan target for the last three years.
evidence.falsification_test: Completions met or exceeded the target in two of the last three years.

evidence.claim: Small sites deliver below their planned share of London homes.
evidence.source_or_test: Check the GLA small sites monitoring against London Plan Policy H2 targets by borough.
evidence.falsification_test: Small-site completions met the Policy H2 target in most boroughs.

evidence.claim: Pre-construction cost for a two-to-ten-home scheme is £60,000 to £90,000 and does not fall with the developer's volume.
evidence.source_or_test: Ten SME developer interviews with cost breakdowns.
evidence.falsification_test: Median reported pre-construction cost falls outside £40,000 to £120,000, or falls by more than 30 per cent for developers doing ten or more schemes a year.

evidence.claim: SME developers will pay a fixed fee for a pre-accepted package.
evidence.source_or_test: Price-stating interviews with ten SME developers.
evidence.falsification_test: Fewer than six of ten state a price at or above the cost floor.

evidence.claim: London's dwelling stock is about 3.7 million.
evidence.source_or_test: Check the DLUHC dwelling stock estimate for London, latest year.
evidence.falsification_test: The published figure differs from 3.7 million by more than 0.3 million.

evidence.claim: Rents fall about 1.5 per cent for each 1 per cent increase in housing stock.
evidence.source_or_test: Literature review of published rent-supply elasticities for UK cities.
evidence.falsification_test: Published estimates cluster outside the range minus 0.5 to minus 3.

evidence.claim: Most small sites in London fall into fewer than ten repeatable site types.
evidence.source_or_test: Classify 200 small-site planning applications from two boroughs.
evidence.falsification_test: More than 30 per cent of sites do not fit any of ten types.

evidence.claim: A borough will accept a standard package in advance for a site type.
evidence.source_or_test: Two borough planning officers asked whether a design code or local development order route is open for a defined site type.
evidence.falsification_test: Both boroughs say no route exists without a plan change.
